content.title: Feature: agt delete issue-id command
content.description: Implement agt delete issue-id command that fully removes an issue and all its references from agentrack. See spec in comments.

content.content: Full spec is in the issue description. See the agentrack spec directory for the detailed implementation guide. Key points: Hard delete of issue and all children. Clean blockages in both directions. Clean mentions for the issue. Delete event file from disk. Return array of all deleted IDs.

content.description: Implement agt delete <issue-id> command that fully removes an issue and all its references from agentrack. Full spec at .agentic/specs/delete-command-spec.md

content.content: Starting implementation. Will follow the spec: types → mentions cleanup → blockages cleanup → tracker method → CLI command → CLI registration.

Done. Implemented the full `agt delete <issue-id>` command as specified:

**Files changed:**
- `types/api.ts` — Added `IssueDeleteParams` and `IssueDeleteResult` types
- `types/index.ts` — Exported new types
- `core/mentions.ts` — Added `removeIssueMentions()` to clean all mentions for an issue
- `core/dependency-manager.ts` — Added `removeAllBlockagesForIssue()` to clean all blockage references for an issue
- `core/tracker.ts` — Added `issueDelete()` method with depth-first cascade delete of descendants
- `cli/commands/delete.ts` — New file, CLI action handler following existing patterns
- `cli/runner.ts` — Registered `delete` command
- `src/index.ts` — Exported new types

**Key implementation details:**
- Descendants collected depth-first (leaves first) for safe deletion order
- Each deleted issue cleans: blockages (both directions), mentions, event file on disk, childrenOf references, and index entries
- Returns array of all deleted IDs in deletion order (children first, target last)
- Auth required (write operation)
- No confirmation prompt (CLI is for agents)
- Works on any status

**Verification:** typecheck ✓, lint ✓, 900/900 existing tests pass (5 pre-existing spec-deviation failures unrelated to this change).
